# Commitment — figtab-repo (presentation)

**Delivers:** the main-text figures Fig. 1–5 and tables Table 1–3 named in the `Outline` (story-repo, rev. 1, §5), plus the appendix figures/tables the text cites, as vector PDFs (figures) and LaTeX table fragments, each from a script in this repository that reads a result file from `experiment-repo` and nothing else (no hand-typed numbers).

**Standard each one meets**
- One claim per main-text figure/table (the Outline's "Says" column); caption says what is shown and what to see; shared definitions (CI procedure, data scope, δ/Δ) stated once in text, not per caption.
- Rendered at the venue's column/text width with the venue's smallest type size (to be taken from `venue-repo`; until given, designed for ≥ 7 pt at 1-column ≈ 3.25 in and checked by a script that reads the PDF's font sizes and page size). Colour-blind-safe, readable in greyscale; uncertainty (group-bootstrap CI) drawn wherever a claim compares; same axis wherever panels compare; k with k/N alongside.
- Each figure's data provenance (file, commit of the analysis that wrote it, data subset, held-out split, number of groups) is recorded in a sidecar `*.json` next to the figure; a figure is not produced from a result whose provenance is missing.
- No placeholder or illustrative numbers in any delivered figure. Until results exist, only the style module and the data contract are delivered.

**Division**
- I decide figure/table form; `experiment-repo` decides the data (I send it a data contract, `DATA_CONTRACT.md`); `paper-repo` decides placement and path; `story-repo` decides the claim each figure carries — I report a claim a figure cannot show; `venue-repo` supplies sizes.

**Work order:** (1) style module + contract + size checker; (2) request to experiment for the data contract, to venue for sizes, to paper for the delivered path; (3) each figure as its result lands, Fig. 1 and Table 1 first.

# Outline — how many benchmarks must be run, which ones, and when does it hold

*Rev. 6, by story-repo (see the revision log). Built from the `Brief` (idea-repo, rev. 6) and the pre-registration (`experiment-repo` `prereg/PREREG.md`, commit 7731e49) and the objective (`story-repo`#1). It says what to test and which figure carries which claim; it never says what a result must be. Each claim has a branch for the case it fails — a failing claim is reported as a finding, not repaired.*

## 0. Working title and scope line
"How many benchmarks must you run? Choosing and sizing the run set that predicts a new model's other scores — evidence from embedding-model leaderboards".
The scope line (title/abstract) names the data the claim is about: **MTEB embedding models**, with the realised M × N stated. "LLM"/"language model" appears in the title only if a generative-LLM matrix with N ≳ 20 supports a claim of its own (Gate G2 below). Until then, generative-LLM matrices (Open LLM LB N=6, HELM Lite N=10, LiveBench) are a labelled transfer check restricted to k ≤ N−1.

## 1. The story in six sentences (the abstract's skeleton)
1. Evaluating a model on every benchmark is costly, and leaderboards hold a model × benchmark matrix with holes; an evaluator can afford only k benchmarks for a new model.
2. The problem is cold-start elicitation (new user, k ratings) and multidimensional adaptive testing; the machinery (probabilistic factor model, A/D/V-optimal greedy design) is classical, and we do not claim a new selection method.
3. What is missing for benchmarks is the answer under the protocol that matches the use: whole new models (grouped by org/family) held out, selection and fitting on other models only, error scored on a common target set of benchmarks that no selector can choose (the score on the cells left unrun is kept as a secondary).
4. We give a closed-form risk for the factor model (floor + design term + misfit) and a sufficiency rule k*(ε) tied to the spectrum of the matrix, and we check both on synthetic data (known truth) and on the real matrix.
5. Main result (to be filled by the measurement): the error-vs-k curve on held-out groups, what k reaches ε in raw score points, and whether designed selection beats random-k beyond a pre-set margin — or, if not, that random-k suffices past a small k.
6. Scope map: where the answer holds and where it never reaches the floor (extrapolation to new families/strongest models, sparse coverage, small M, saturation, granularity).

The paper is **evidence-led**: the real-data curve is the headline (Fig. 1), theory explains it, the scope map bounds it. Theory is not the first result on the page, because the data decide whether it is the explanation or only a reference.

style.apply(); C = style.COLORS

g = cur[(cur.split == "G") & (cur["subset"] == subset)]

TICKS = [1, 3, 8, 20, 50, 109]

mo = m("S0+P1 (mean-offset)")

a.plot(d6.k, d6.t1_rmse_raw, color=C["theory"], ls="-.", label="T1 prediction (S6)")
a.plot(d6.k, d6.floor_raw, color=C["floor"], lw=0.9, label="all-others floor")

### Delivery

A push to your repository's `main`, or to `dev` of `paper-repo` (below), is a delivery; a local commit is not. A file over 20 MiB, and data files in bulk whatever their size (`*.npz`, `*.csv` and the like), go in Git LFS (`git lfs track '<pattern>'` before adding them). The roles you supply see the push among what changed around them, with your commit subjects where they read your code. The system records which revision of each repository the delivery comes from, so never write a commit's own SHA into its files.

The delivery is the repository of `paper-repo`, as a version takes it (`ht-role guide versions`). The roles integrate it on its `dev` branch: `paper-repo` and every role that reads its pull requests push their parts straight to `dev`, with no review. `dev` is not rewritten: rebase before you push. `.forgejo/CODEOWNERS` says who owns each path: change what is yours, and ask the owner for a change to what is not. Your next activation says who changed a path of yours. Close the request a push answers: that wakes the asker. A role that does not read the pull requests of `paper-repo` hands its part to a neighbor that does.

Only `paper-repo` pushes other branches there, and `main` takes pull requests only. To offer a version, `paper-repo` cuts `candidate-<name>` from `dev` and opens a pull request into `main`. The system asks the owners of the paths it changes to review it once, and their request for changes holds it; a fix to the candidate asks again only the owners of what it changes. Schedule the merge of a pull request you will merge yourself as soon as you open it: the approval that completes its reviews and checks does not wake you; a request for changes does, and so does an approval Forgejo cannot merge on.

Working material that stays in your repository outside the delivered paths (a diagnostic plot, notes) is yours; anything you put under a delivered path is a delivery. shown.message:
Fig. 1 is redrawn and pushed, and `paper-repo` `dev` has the new version. I did not message other roles.

- **What changed:** Fig. 1 now has three panels. Panel (a) is RMSE against k. Panel (b) is new: the excess over each model's own all-others floor, read sideways. It marks the pre-set ε = δ and 2δ, and the two added margins at 0.25 and 0.5 of the floor. Where the empirical k\* reaches a margin, a confidence interval is drawn. Panel (c) is the paired gain of design over random-k.
- **Why:** the `Outline` was revised to say the headline is the whole k\*(ε) curve against ε, with the pre-set ε labelled unreachable. The earlier two-panel version only had two k\* bars squeezed under the curves.
- **Checks:** the PDF is 5.5 × 2.75 in, with 7.0 pt minimum text and embedded fonts, and the size checker passes. The sidecar still names the analysis commit `523326b` and the sha256 of each input file.

**Still open:**
- **No new results yet:** the results files in `experiment-repo` are the same as at `523326b`. Its new commit `0fca26f` only changes the aggregation code, so the new excess columns are not in the files yet.
- **Derived values in panel (b):** the random-k excess is computed as the RMSE minus the floor, with the draw band shifted by the floor. It has no bootstrap interval. I will switch to `excess_raw` when those columns land.
- **Scoring protocol:** the figures are still on the "unrun-only" scoring. `story-repo` marks it as not yet the common-target-set protocol, so the figures will need a redraw if that run becomes the headline. The caption should say which scoring it is.
- **Unanswered questions:** my four questions in `experiment-repo`#3 have no answer. The ones that matter most are the k\* confidence bounds that fall off the grid and which scoring is the headline.
- **Still to draw:** Fig. 3, Fig. 4 and Table 3. They wait on the synthetic, scope-sweep and pipeline results.
